To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of an increase in government expenditure is negative if it is financed by an increase in money supply, and positive if it is financed through an increase in income taxes.
(i) in a closed economy, the effect of government expenditure is not necessarily expansionary and that (ii) the effect of an increase in money supply is not necessarily contractionary.

the effect of a fiscal expansion on investment and output depends crucially on how it is financed and that the effect of monetary expansion on output depends crucially not only on how it is implemented, but also on the state of the economy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamic path of a dynamic macroeconomic framework with two uses of credit.
the role of the financial sector and the policy variables, viz. money supply, government expenditure and taxes, in the context of a developing country.
the dynamic effects of monetary and fiscal policy on the real sector and banks and also with the dynamic effects on the real sector of credit rationing and credit crunch.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study are in line with those of the earlier studies.
in the short run the effect of monetary policy on the economy is more important than that of fiscal policy.
the model is a useful device in the hands of a policy-maker to explore the effects of alternative policies in a bad state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in a bad state the government should finance its increased expenditures by raising income taxes and not by deficit financing.
the model has a number of interesting results which are contrary to the received wisdom.
in the long-run the effect of fiscal policy on investment is negative and in the short-run the effect is positive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the government expenditure should be financed by raising taxes rather than by deficit financing.
in a dynamic setting, the effect of policy on the long-term interest rate and investment depends on the financing of the policy.
the policy mix is very important and the policy maker has to choose the right one.
